statute_check.summary: FAILS bar (c) prospectively. Tennessee Public Chapter 1044 (2026; SB 2237; new T.C.A. 7-51-2204) applies to site plans and takes effect 2027-01-01 for plans submitted on/after that date. It requires written staff comments within 30 business days, caps written deficiency notices at two, and (subsection (e)) requires the local government to notify the developer in writing within 30 business days if a submission is incomplete; the clocks restart only on a new complete submittal. That is a statutory pre-review written incompleteness loop of the kind TIERS.md says to avoid (like FL/GA/CA/AZ). Before 2027-01-01 no TN statute mandated it: the only earlier submittal-linked rule is the vesting statute T.C.A. 13-4-310 (as amended 2025), under which rights vest on submission of a plan that 'substantially complies' (a vesting trigger, not a hold). Official act PDF (publications.tnsosfiles.com/acts/114/pub/pc1044.pdf) did not download (HTML returned); quotes are from the UT CLP policy guide and the UT MTAS/CLP FAQ.

research.reason: Practice is Tier 3: the MPC/SALDO clock runs from receipt (the staff briefing computes the 90-day review deadline from the submission date), plans go on the next PC agenda before the engineer's first letter, and missing items (the SS155.029(C) improvement certification, the financial-security election, stormwater for an unshown gravel lot, NPDES) surface in PC/BOS review and end in tabling or conditional approval; 44 BOS + 13 PC minutes show no refusal. But the township's own words carry hold language: the planning page conditions agenda placement on 'Complete proposals', and the form warns of 'refusals to process' and has a 5-item required list. Read literally under TIERS (written hold + list, enforcement irrelevant) that is Tier 1; read as a deadline rule with a soft warning it is Tier 3. Not golden-set safe either way; Will should rule.
